item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B is substantially closer to the frozen contract, especially in its exact public API and reuse of multipartbody.NewFile. Candidate A introduces several explicitly forbidden API and scope changes.","reasons":["B implements the required Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) signature; A instead exposes opts ...UploadFileOption, violating the exact API contract and changing FilesOption behavior.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile directly. A adds duplicate NewForm machinery and association-field options, despite the contract explicitly forbidding association fields.","A bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request/response handling, while also refactoring unrelated RawClient retry behavior. B at least centralizes shared behavior in a private add helper, though it still does not literally route Upload through Add.","B verifies multipart field name, filename, content, and retry behavior. A also tests these well, including retry from a non-seekable source, but those strengths do not outweigh its major contract violations and broad scope expansion."],"risks_a":["The public Upload signature is wrong and introduces a parallel option system.","Adds association APIs and multipart NewForm support explicitly outside the requested scope.","Duplicates Add's request construction, decoding, and missing-data error handling instead of routing through Add, risking future divergence and subtly different option semantics/order handling due to the separate option type and wrapper API surface, even if the immediate Raw.Do call looks similar in the visible diff; the architectural duplication itself is the concrete concern visible here rather than a proven current mismatch in specific errors or options. Also refactors RawClient replay behavior globally, creating unnecessary risk around shared seekers and concurrent/repeated request-body access; the shared seeker in GetBody is mutable and could be unsafe if transports access retries or redirects in unexpected patterns. Source-reader failure behavior is not directly tested."],"risks_b":["Changes Add to eagerly buffer every caller-built multipart body, contrary to preserving its existing behavior and lower-level nature; this changes memory, timing, streaming, and reader-error semantics.","Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the existing public Add method, missing the contract's explicit single-path requirement.","Tests do not cover empty-filename validation, nil content, non-seekable streamed input, or source-reader failures."]}
